author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Split a large EmuCoreX library into non-overlapping roots
summary: Design internal, SD-card, and temporary roots with explicit ownership, move one collection segment at a time, prevent parent-child overlap, and reconcile physical-image counts with EmuCoreX entries.
heroAlt: PCSX2 data-directory configuration screen illustrating separate named locations for emulator content

blocks.text: Give every root one reason to exist

Multiple roots are useful when fast internal storage holds demanding titles and an SD card holds the rest. They become harmful when a selected parent contains another selected root, when backups sit under a playable folder, or when the same image is copied to both locations without a deliberate transition. Define the boundary on paper before selecting anything in Android's picker.
Never add both PS2 and PS2/Favorites as roots. EmuCoreX will legitimately discover the same image through both trees, and deleting one duplicate entry can be mistaken for deleting one of two files.
Draft a root map with counts

items: A list of currently authorized roots and the storage device behind each URI.
A deduplicated inventory of personal images by SHA-256.
A grouping rule such as performance tier, region, or physical device.
No backup, download, extraction, or quarantine folder nested under a proposed root.
Enough free capacity to move one group while retaining its source copy.

blocks.text: Introduce roots one at a time

items: 1. Choose the smallest collection group and create an empty destination folder directly under its intended storage volume.
2. Copy that group, verify its hashes, and confirm that no corresponding image remains in another active root unless it is still part of the migration.
3. Authorize only the destination folder through the Android tree picker.
4. Refresh EmuCoreX and compare new entries with the group's inventory before adding another root.
5. Cold-boot one title from the beginning, middle, and end of the group to test provider traversal rather than one cached file.
6. Remove the group's old root or old files only after the new root survives an app restart.
7. Repeat for the next group, keeping a table of root URI display name, physical volume, purpose, image count, and verification date.

blocks.text: A region subfolder can organize files without becoming a separate selected root. Select the highest non-overlapping folder that contains only playable material. If one storage device is removed, EmuCoreX should report only that device's root unavailable while titles on other roots remain intact.
The final count must be explained rather than merely close. Multidisc sets, cue/bin components, and intentionally separate revisions require notes.

items: No authorized root is an ancestor or descendant of another authorized root.
Each verified image hash appears in exactly one active root.
Removing the SD card affects only entries assigned to that card.
Favorites and per-game profiles still resolve to the intended serial.
Every root retains its Android permission after restart.
Every title appears twice after adding one folder: inspect for parent-child overlap.
A refresh scans archives or temporary files: quarantine is nested inside an active root.
One card removal empties the whole library: all entries may have been assigned through one broad parent.
Two regional revisions collapse into one label: verify serials before treating them as duplicate files.

blocks.text: Remove the newest root without moving content

Revoke or remove only the last folder selection, refresh once, and confirm the earlier roots recover their original counts. Keep destination files in place while diagnosing the map; moving them again would add a second variable. Re-authorize the corrected non-overlapping root after the inventory is consistent.
Provider names are not unique identifiers

Two SD cards can present the same volume label, and Android can change a document URI after a reformat. Record capacity, folder contents, and physical device alongside the visible name so future maintenance does not grant the wrong tree.
